subject: Performance acceptance playbook and load test schedule
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Handoff: Fabled Health — performance acceptance asks

Hi team,

Quick handoff: Fabled Health (Evelyn & Rajiv) confirmed they want a formal performance acceptance run during onboarding. They care most about end-to-end latency at p95 and steady-state throughput for their nightly batching jobs. Sales scoped the ask in discovery but we need CS/implementation to own the runbook.

Key bullets from discovery:
- Target p95 for small interactive requests (~150 tokens) <= 220 ms network-to-first-token, p50 <= 80 ms.
- Throughput target for batch ingestion: 12k tokens/sec sustained for 30 minutes on their Dedicated slot.
- Peak concurrency expected during test: 40 concurrent sessions (short chat style).

Attached: fabled-load-specs.xlsx (sales notes + customer expectations).

Can CS pick this up and propose a concrete test window and acceptance criteria? I copied Marcus for infra-assisted tuning.

Thanks,
Steph
— Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Handoff: Fabled Health — performance acceptance asks

Thanks Steph — picking this up.

Laura/Monica, proposed approach below (high level) — please review and flag gaps:

1) Test plan (staging -> dedicated)
   - Phase A: Staging run to validate harness and baseline (Locust-based). 15m ramp, 30m steady, 15m cool-down.
   - Phase B: Dedicated trial on their reserved pool (if they can provision test capacity) — 10m smoke, 60m steady.

2) Load profile
   - Interactive: 40 concurrent sessions, mean request size 150 tokens, token distribution attached in fabled-load-specs.xlsx.
   - Batch: single-job injection at start of steady window to target 12k tokens/sec sustained for 30 mins.

3) Metrics & success criteria
   - p50/p95 latency (network-to-first-token and total-response), error rate <= 0.5%  
   - Throughput: sustain 12k tokens/sec for 30m (batch) AND maintain interactive p95 <= 250 ms (allowable if dedicated warmed).
   - No model OOMs or degraded quantization fallbacks during run.

4) Observability and artifacts to share
   - Locust raw logs, APM spans (trace ids), token-level cost breakdown from Console, and summarized CSV (see baseline-latency-snapshot-20260315.csv).

5) Responsibilities
   - Redwood infra (Marcus): kernel profile and autoscaling knobs, pre-warm KV cache, select quantization profile.
   - CS (Laura/Monica): run harness, coordinate windows with customer, share results, and iterate prompts if needed.
   - Sales (Steph): procurement sign-off for dedicated test capacity and SOW gap.

6) Schedule (proposal)
   - Staging run: 2026-03-17 10:00–11:30 PT
   - Dedicated run (tentative): 2026-03-18 14:00–16:00 PT

Please confirm availability and any run constraints from infra side. I'll draft an external mail to coordinate windows.

— Soojin
So?jin Lee
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Turner <evelyn.turner@fabledhealth.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@fabledhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-16T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Scheduling acceptance runs — proposed windows and checklist

Hi Evelyn / Rajiv,

Thanks again for partnering with Redwood. Per our discovery, we'd like to run two short acceptance exercises to validate latency and throughput before final sign-off. Below is a concrete checklist and two proposed windows; let us know which works best or suggest alternatives.

Quick checklist (what we'll need from Fabled Health):
- Staging API key and test workload (we can replay a sample of your nightly job).
- Whitelisted test IPs for dedicated run, or a short VPN tunnel (ops@fabledhealth.com can coordinate).
- Point of contact on the day for immediate triage (either Rajiv or Evelyn).

Proposed windows (PT):
- Staging run: 2026-03-17 10:00–11:30 (internal only; no SLA implications)
- Dedicated run: 2026-03-18 14:00–16:00 (this will use reserved capacity; please confirm if you can provision a test slot)

Acceptance criteria summary:
- Interactive p95 <= 250 ms (network to first token) for 150-token inputs
- Batch throughput >= 12k tokens/sec sustained for 30m
- Error rate <= 0.5%

Attachments: initial-load-plan.yml (test harness config)

If that works, Monica will run the tests and share the CSV + traces afterwards.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@fabledhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Turner <evelyn.turner@fabledhealth.com>
Cc: ops@fabledhealth.com, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-17T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Scheduling acceptance runs — proposed windows and checklist

Thanks Laura — we can do the staging run tomorrow morning. A couple of clarifications:

On 2026-03-16 08:22, Laura Bennett wrote:
> Acceptance criteria summary:
> - Interactive p95 <= 250 ms (network to first token) for 150-token inputs
> - Batch throughput >= 12k tokens/sec sustained for 30m
> - Error rate <= 0.5%

Two notes from our infra team:
1) Our staging environment adds ~40 ms to end-to-end latency compared with our production network. Please include that as a delta when you share p95 numbers.
2) For the dedicated run: we can provision a test slot but need the Redwood team to run a dry-start (10m) to confirm the KV cache warm-up procedure. Also: can you avoid changing quantization mid-run? That caused a hiccup in a previous engagement.

We'll have ops@fabledhealth.com available to open IPs and a Slack channel during the run. Confirming staging 2026-03-17 10:00 PT.

— Rajiv
CTO, Fabled Health
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Turner <evelyn.turner@fabledhealth.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@fabledhealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Results: staging baseline + next steps for dedicated run

Hi all — quick summary after today's staging run (10:00–10:45 PT):

What we ran
- Locust harness replaying a 30-min excerpt of your nightly batch + interactive clients (40 concurrent).
- Warmed KV cache for 10m before steady window.

Key results (staging, numbers include client-observed network delta noted by Rajiv):
- Interactive: p50 = 72 ms, p95 = 215 ms (network-to-first-token)
- Batch: peak sustained throughput = 11.8k tokens/sec over a 28-minute window (just shy of 12k target)
- Error rate: 0.12% (primarily transient 429s during ramp)

Notes and recommended actions before dedicated run
- We saw a small 2–4% drop during a quantization fallback event at minute 17 of steady state; Marcus will pin the quantization profile to avoid mid-run changes.
- Slightly increase instance pre-warm (extra 2 minutes) to help hit the 12k/sec target.

Artifacts attached: baseline-latency-snapshot-20260315.csv (raw timing), test-results-20260318.csv (locust summary). We'll upload full traces to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBfabledTestPlan

Next steps
- Marcus: apply pinned quantization and bump pre-warm; can you confirm by 2026-03-18 10:00 PT?
- Fabled: confirm dedicated slot provisioning and an ops contact for a 14:00 PT start.
- Monica & Soojin: we'll run the dedicated window and share a formal pass/fail report within 3 hours of completion.

Happy to hop on a quick 15-min call before the dedicated run if anyone wants to walk the checklist.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: test-results-20260318.csv
